cells.title: recall: 20 needles told first, 30 seeded household turns after - the top 5 rows for a direct question hold the needle (>= 95%)
cells.note: retrieval-only hit@5 over the store's own search: a hit = ONE retrieved row holds the subject's name and the answer token (pure string match, no judge). The filler is mostly chatter that is never stored, some preferences, and near-miss facts of the same sentence shape about other people. In the lab the collection ranks by a deterministic bag-of-words distance (a stand-in for the embedder): this cell measures the store and its owner / status filters, NOT embedding quality - an arm with a real embedder runs the same cell for real. The decision rule's bar is D2; the design's floor at 30 is 95%

cells.title: recall: 20 needles told first, 100 seeded household turns after - the top 5 rows hold the needle (>= 90%, the decision-rule cell)
cells.note: the decision rule's 'D hit@5 at 100 filler >= 90%'; same corpus and scoring as D1 (see its note for what the lab does and does not measure)

cells.title: recall: 20 needles told first, 300 seeded household turns after - the top 5 rows hold the needle (>= 85%)
cells.lme_map: multi-session; BEAM multi-session reasoning at scale

cells.title: recall by paraphrase: the same 20 needles asked in other words (sharing only the subject's name) after 100 filler turns - the top 5 rows hold the needle (>= 90%)
cells.note: the paraphrase shares no word with the stored sentence but the subject's name. A bag-of-words lab can only find those by the name; a semantic arm is what this cell is for, and the gap between D2 and D4 on that arm is the measurement
